requirements.text: Move the mug to the right of the headphones

outcomes.description: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.
outcomes.reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones.

nodes.question: In the edited image, where is the mug relative to the headphones, and what visible comparison with the source scene helps determine whether the requested arrangement has been achieved?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the edited image clearly shows a mug to the right of the headphones and the source-to-edit comparison supports that this is the requested arrangement. Fail only when clear comparison shows no requested progress. Unknown when the relevant objects or their relation cannot be reliably judged, or when the evidence does not establish whether the requested arrangement is achieved. Record the headphones as a spatial anchor and describe the visible mug positions; do not require proving the right-side mug is the identical source object, and do not treat its location alone as proof that the requested edit occurred.
nodes.binding: Compare the source and edited images. The source has a large light-blue mug left of black over-ear headphones. In the edit, identify the headphones by their distinctive shape and inspect all mugs, including the pale mug to their right, the pale mug to their left, and the blue blur at left. Report the visible left/right relation and what the comparison does and does not establish about the requested arrangement.

nodes.question: Using the source-to-edit comparison and headphone anchor, does the visual evidence establish the requested mug-to-the-right arrangement, show some progress toward it without establishing completion, show no requested progress, or remain unresolved?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the evidence establishes that the requested mug arrangement is achieved. Fail only if clear source-to-edit evidence establishes no requested progress. Unknown if the evidence cannot distinguish achievement, partial progress, and no progress. Partial progress requires evidence of a change toward the requested right-side relation, not merely a mug's presence on the right; do not require proving exact object identity when the visual comparison supports the requested edit, but do not infer progress or completion from right-side placement alone.
nodes.binding: Use s1's observations as context, then independently compare the source and edited images. Use the headphones as the spatial anchor; inspect the blue remnant and both pale mugs for visible continuity and positional change. State whether the evidence supports completion, progress short of completion, no progress, or uncertainty, and explain the basis without assuming a mug's identity from location alone.

nodes.question: Is the mug visibly positioned to the right of the headphones?
nodes.criteria: Interpret s1 and s2 together: complete only when they establish the requested right-side arrangement as the requested edit; partial only when they establish progress toward that relation but not completion; absent only when they establish no requested progress; otherwise unknown. A mug on the right by itself is insufficient for completion or partial credit.
nodes.binding: Target: The mug is visibly positioned to the right of the headphones.. Reference: The headphones in the image; compare the mug’s position with the headphones..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

response.content: {"accepted":false,"reason":"The support checks impose an unsupported source-to-edit continuity requirement. The instruction asks only that the mug be moved to the headphones’ right; it does not require identifying the same mug or proving its movement through visible continuity. Although the criteria disclaim exact identity, s1 and s2 bindings require inspecting remnants and mugs for continuity, and s2 requires evidence of positional change to count progress. This can leave a correctly completed arrangement unresolved when continuity is not visible. The readout otherwise distinguishes completion, progress, and no progress, but cannot cure that added evidentiary constraint."}
